gap: No result ChatGPT got puts a number on how slow the relay fallback is. QNAP's own figure for its myQNAPcloud Link relay is 1–2 Mbps. At that speed one 1 GB phone video takes about 67–133 minutes to pull. Tailscale measured about 2.2 Mbps through its DERP relay, which is about 61 minutes per GB. Neither Synology, UGREEN nor Asustor publishes a relay speed at all.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and cited no pages, so the only thing to compare against is its own answer. That answer says only that a relay is 'potentially slower' and that a direct connection is 'often faster', with no figure for either. Our current page has QNAP's 1–2 Mbps, but it cites the wrong page: the myQNAPcloud FAQ it links only says QNAP will 'monitor the bandwidth and enforce some limits if necessary'. The number comes from QNAP's 2026-04-07 reference article, and that article ties it to shared global bandwidth, not to peak hours. None of the pages turns a speed into transfer time, and none has Tailscale's measured DERP number.
decides: This confirms that the pick should depend on getting a direct path, not on which brand's relay you use. Every vendor relay that publishes a number or has been measured runs at about 1–2 Mbps. That works for opening a document or a single photo. It is not workable for pulling video or catching up a photo backup. Behind CGNAT, favor a NAS that can run Tailscale (UGREEN DXP2800 through Docker, Synology DS225+/DS223j through the official package, QNAP through Container Station) or that offers an IPv6 direct path, and treat the vendor relay as a last resort. The DH2300 has no Docker, so it is weaker here unless you add a separate Tailscale device.

findings.label: Measured throughput through the DERP relay vs a peer relay
findings.value: DERP ≈2.2 Mbps sustained; peer relay 27.5 Mbps (27–35 Mbps)
findings.source_title: Tailscale blog: peer relays on international networks (2026-01-26)
findings.note: 120 s iperf3 TCP test from Delhi, India to Robbinsdale, MN. DERP receiver 2.20 Mbps; Tailscale credits 'DERP QoS shaping'. This is one intercontinental path, not a published cap. A US domestic DERP path may be faster.

findings.label: Time to pull one 1 GB video at the measured DERP rate
findings.value: ≈61 min (vs ≈4.8 min via peer relay at 27.5 Mbps)
findings.source_title: Tailscale blog: peer relays on international networks
findings.note: 8,000 Mb ÷ 2.2 Mbps = 3,636 s ≈ 61 min; 8,000 ÷ 27.5 = 291 s ≈ 4.8 min. When Tailscale gets a direct connection, speed is limited only by the home's upload.

unsourced: Relay speed for UGREENlink: no figure on nas.ugreen.com or support pages, and no named reviewer measured it (igor'sLAB, Macwelt and NASCompares describe it without numbers). I found only one anonymous Reddit report of 'KB/s' speeds.

Relay speed for Synology QuickConnect: the DSM 7.4 spec says only 'may be slower'. The KB article on Drive speed did not render, and the QuickConnect white paper was not reachable. I found only anonymous forum reports (1.4 MB/s, 52 Mbit).
Relay speed for Asustor EZ-Connect: the help page confirms it is rate-limited but gives no number.
A US-to-US Tailscale DERP throughput figure: the only measured number is Tailscale's own Delhi-to-Minnesota test.

An official Apple figure for MB per minute of iPhone 4K HEVC video, to turn the per-GB times into per-clip times: only third-party estimates (170–400 MB/min) turned up, so I used 1 GB and 100 MB as the units instead.
Amazon prices for Synology DS225+/DS223j and QNAP TS-264: amzcheck.py search returned nothing (likely walled), and neither maker has a US store I could check.
